findings.summary: _brand star-imports _logo without _logo.__all__, leaking implementation/dependency names; package __all__ simultaneously omits the logo API.
Logo CLI docs/prog advertise python -m scikitplot.logo, but no scikitplot.logo module exists.
Eager package imports preload executable _banner/_logo modules, producing runpy already-in-sys.modules warnings on direct module execution.
Banner batch generation can skip every generation failure and return an empty mapping; main still returns success for that zero-output batch.

The Eukrina Mind AI brand existed only as a generated bundle of 410 recoloured PNGs: one-colour symbols merged the diagonal into the U and were misnamed (forest = taupe, navy = charcoal), the diagonal left the round icon's circle, the mark sat 7 units off centre, gradient ids collided between documents, and light-background accents and subtitles missed WCAG contrast (2.0-3.4:1). Retired by scikitplot._brand._kit and scikitplot._brand._eukrina (PR 949): the brand as data, drawn by rule to safe SVG, contrast-safe colours, a gap in one-colour marks, idempotent builds with a checksummed manifest. Honest limit: SVG only in this increment; live text depends on the viewer's fonts (outline mode does not).

scikitplot/_brand/_banner.py line 574 evaluates collections.abc.Callable[[str], str] at import time; on Python 3.8 this raises TypeError, so scikitplot._brand (logo, banner, kit and Eukrina) cannot be imported on the oldest supported Python. Found during PR 949; not changed there.
